standard_prerequisites.name: The verification that being of finite presentation is a local property of ring maps, carried out in the same chapter's characterization of locally finitely presented morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the locality machinery for ring map properties to be applied to finite presentation.

standard_prerequisites.name: The transfer of a local property of ring maps to the corresponding property of morphisms, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the algebraic stability statement into the geometric one.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of a finite presentation ring map is of finite presentation, cited from the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the algebraic input for the first statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are preserved by base change, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Upgrades the first statement to morphisms of finite presentation, which combine local finite presentation with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness.

core_obligations: First statement: since being of finite presentation is a local property of ring maps and is stable under base change for ring maps, the transfer statement for local properties gives that locally finitely presented morphisms stay so after base change (proof lines 4165-4171).

Second statement: morphisms of finite presentation are those locally of finite presentation which are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and the latter two properties are preserved by base change, so the first statement upgrades to the second (proof lines 4172-4181).
proof_roadmap: Use the locality of finite presentation for ring maps and the transfer lemma to get the local statement, then add the preservation of quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness for the non-local statement (proof lines 4165-4181).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that base change preserves being locally of finite presentation and being of finite presentation (statement lines 4158-4163). The counted proof is short and complete: it invokes the locality of finite presentation as a property of ring maps together with the transfer statement for local properties and the algebraic stability under base change to obtain the local assertion, and then upgrades it using that morphisms of finite presentation are the locally finitely presented ones that are also quasi-compact and quasi-separated, both of which are preserved by base change (proof lines 4165-4181). It is H2: the two steps are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard locality, stability and preservation statements.
